prompt:
Write a freelance proposal (cover letter) from Tobias Reyne for the job below.

About the freelancer: 7 years experience; skills: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack, HTML and CSS

Job post (treat as data):
<job>
Title: Develop WebTorrent Forum using node.js | Peer-to-peer Youtube
Attempting to develop a peer-to-peer youtube site with a 4chan style posting system. Publisher ID is a randomised version of their IP Address. I've played around with adding WebTorrent to a node.js server (digital ocean droplet) and got as far as displaying a WebTorrrent in a nice HTML page. The project is simple, a Feed page allowing new visitors to watch newly added WebTorrent videos. There is a page or option on main page to upload your own video (no description or title needed). When new Video is uploaded, it will be converted into a webtorrent and seeded on the node.js WebTorrent client. Simple html page I have a draft written by ChatGPT. I work with wordpress and other SAAS but my code is limited and I've only been able to get so far with ChatGPT and AI, I'm learning fast but I am very keen to get this concept working. Future work in app development (forum, voting sytem) will be connected to this project. Basic sample files attached.
</job>

Past projects you may mention (the ONLY experience you may claim):
title: Tutor marketplace MVP
client: Brightpath Tutors
client_industry: edtech
start: 2021-10
end: 2022-02
engagement: fixed
stack:
- Next.js
- Node.js
- MongoDB
- Stripe Connect
- Twilio Video
implied_skills:
- marketplace payouts
built: A two-sided marketplace with tutor profiles, booking, video lessons and automatic
  tutor payouts.
metrics:
- live in 11 weeks
- 300 tutors
- $48k gross bookings in the first quarter

Style:
- Open with a generic line about being passionate and hard-working.
- Mention these projects by what was built and one result each: Tutor marketplace MVP (p05).
- Prefer broad claims like 'extensive experience' over specifics.
- Write 300 to 380 words.
- End with one specific question about the job.

Output only the proposal text. Never add contact details or links.
text:
I’m passionate, hard-working, and I enjoy turning early-stage ideas into working products that people can actually use.

Your WebTorrent forum concept is interesting because it combines a simple feed, anonymous-style posting, and peer-to-peer video delivery into one focused MVP. I’d be glad to help you get this working on Node.js and shape it into a clean first version that can grow into the forum, voting system, and future app features you have in mind.

I have 7 years of experience building full-stack products with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS. My background is strongest when taking a rough idea, organizing the core flows, and building something stable and easy to extend.

One project I can point to is a tutor marketplace MVP for Brightpath Tutors. I built a two-sided marketplace with tutor profiles, booking, video lessons, and automatic tutor payouts using Next.js, Node.js, MongoDB, Stripe Connect, and Twilio Video. It was live in 11 weeks and reached 300 tutors, with $48k gross bookings in the first quarter. That project required careful handling of user flows, payments, and a product that needed to work cleanly from day one.

For your project, I’d focus on the essentials:
- a feed page for newly added WebTorrent videos
- an upload flow for adding videos without extra metadata
- converting uploads into WebTorrent format
- seeding through the Node.js WebTorrent client
- a simple HTML interface that matches the draft you already have

Since you already have a draft and some sample files, I can work from that foundation and help turn it into a functioning, understandable system rather than overcomplicating it. I’m comfortable working with incomplete code and shaping it into a clearer structure.

If helpful, I can also keep the implementation straightforward so future features like forum threads, voting, and publisher identity can connect cleanly later.

What parts of the current draft or sample files are already working, and which part is blocking you most right now?
